reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily explains how to sell products globally on eBay from India, including account documentation and payment procedures. It also advertises export-import and e-commerce mentorship through a website and WhatsApp contact, but the described material does not include a deceptive mechanism or a payment-for-guaranteed-return scheme. References to obtaining orders and building a good business are presented as general e-commerce advice, without established guaranteed earnings, actual outcomes, or deceptive intent.

opening.argument: The central pitch links a simple viewer action to a concrete business and income outcome. After explaining that a seller can create listings and regularly update products, the speaker says, "You can do 60 preseyings And your business will be very good You can earn new orders" and that "if you do your listing the orders will also come, you just have to update regular products on eBay." This is more than neutral platform instruction: it presents listing activity as the route to orders and a good business, making the promised return the reason to participate. The low-effort framing strengthens the solicitation because the stated process is presented as straightforward rather than materially uncertain.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this general advice does not answer the unusually direct wording: the speaker says the business will be very good and orders will come if viewers list and update products. That is an outcome linked to an instructed action, not merely an explanation of account documentation. The defense also overlooks that the video repeatedly directs viewers toward further participation rather than limiting itself to platform mechanics.

citations.quote: You can do 60 preseyings And your business will be very good You can earn new orders
if you do your listing the orders will also come, you just have to update regular products on eBay

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those statements still do not establish guaranteed income, deception, or a payment-for-return scheme. They describe potential orders from operating an actual e-commerce listing, while the same material explains fees, documentation, shipping, and payment processing. Saying listings can produce orders is not equivalent to promising a fixed or effortless payout.

opening.argument: Several concrete signals make the income message function as a solicitation. The speaker pairs claims that listing is easy and produces orders with a direct funnel to an outside website, WhatsApp number, and paid training. The description invites viewers to contact the promoter for "Mentorship, consultancy , Classroom program or Online training regarding Export Import & Ecommerce Business," while the video says viewers can earn new orders through regular listing. The frame-based prompts repeatedly say to visit the website or WhatsApp, including a request to join online training. That combination of an attractive business outcome, an external contact route, and an early-bird fee is a meaningful warning sign that viewers are being steered toward participation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the promotional elements as incidental, but the external website and WhatsApp route are displayed and spoken as the next step, alongside an early-bird fee increase. That urgency matters because it encourages contact or registration while the video highlights business and order prospects. The issue is the combined solicitation structure, not whether every e-commerce fact is false.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: External contact information and an early-bird training offer show promotion, but they do not show that viewers are promised a guaranteed return or that the training is fraudulent. The e-commerce outcome is not tied to buying the course; it is discussed in the context of listing products on eBay. The visible prompts establish advertising, not deception.

opening.argument: Although presented as education, the video's operational explanation also serves as a sales presentation for the speaker's own services. The description advertises mentorship, consultancy, classroom and online programs, and the on-screen frame explicitly says, "Online or Offline Export & Import Training Visit www.AnkitSahu.com." The speaker closes by directing interested viewers to register and mentions a discount before fees increase. Against that promotional backdrop, claims that eBay is easy, that business will be very good, and that orders will come encourage viewers to pursue the offered pathway. The instructional format therefore makes the solicitation appear authoritative while steering viewers toward contact and paid participation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The label of instruction cannot neutralize the video's commercial function. The speaker does not merely explain eBay; he directs interested viewers to register for his training, advertises a fee increase, and displays the website and WhatsApp route. The eBay advice supplies credibility for that funnel, while the promised business outcome supplies motivation to enter it.

citations.quote: those who are interested register in it because there is an early bird offer after that my fees will increase as per the standard fees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion of a training service does not by itself convert operational education into a scam. The material identifies ordinary account requirements and explains that sellers must handle shipping and platform fees. Nothing cited shows that purchasing training is required to obtain eBay orders, nor does it establish a guaranteed return, false identity, or fabricated result.
